title: Grain Bowl
summary: 2000s café format — ancient grains meet modern macro bowls.
origins: The composed grain bowl as a restaurant category exploded in U.S. coastal cities circa 2010–2015 (Sweetgreen, Dig, local café culture). Its DNA is older: Japanese donburi, Korean bibimbap, Hawaiian poke bowls, and Andean quinoa plates all stack starch + protein + vegetables + sauce.
history: Instagram-era food photography made bowls visual shorthand for "healthy." Quinoa bowls specifically rode the 2013 UN Year of Quinoa and wellness trend. Home versions are essentially intentional leftovers — a format, not a fixed recipe.
first_known: Café trend ~2010s; antecedents thousands of years old
teaching: Warm the base — cold grain kills the eating experience.
Sauce is the personality; season each layer, not just the top.
Crunch last: nuts, seeds, or pickled veg on top.
fun_fact: Bowl meals became a thing because everything tastes better when the fork path is shorter.
